messages:
Incident Bot: Postmortem thread created for INC-2025-02-16 (Dedicated burst beta) — elevated tail latency + burst circuit breaker oscillation. Please add findings + action items here.

Rafael Mendes: Dropping quick summary from today’s review so we can converge on action items for GA hardening. This is focused on circuit breaker behavior + guardrails (not general capacity sizing).

Rafael Mendes: Impact recap:
- Window: ~11:18–11:33 PT
- Scope: us-east / H100 shared burst pool (beta)
- Symptom: non-burst tenants saw p95 and p99 latency jump (mostly tail amplification), plus increased 429s from gateway for a subset of burst traffic.
- We also saw the global circuit breaker flapping (open/close cycles) which made the behavior hard to reason about.

Sean Gallagher: +1. From oncall perspective, the breaker “helped” but was noisy and late. Primary SLO we’re protecting is non-burst Dedicated latency; we need the breaker to be earlier + monotonic (once open, stay open for a minimum).

Peter Holtz: Root behavior as seen from routing:
- Admission controller started denying w/ `FLEET_SAFETY_CAP` and `POOL_SATURATED` intermittently.
- Routing fell back to baseline capacity but got a mix of “retry soon” vs “hard deny” semantics depending on which path the request hit.
- Resulted in burst clients doing retries that amplified load right as the breaker toggled.

Keiko Yamamoto: From guardrails side, the flapping looks tied to two signals we used in the breaker:
1) pool saturation computed from allocator telemetry (laggy)
2) p95 delta for neighbor impact (fast-ish but noisy)
When telemetry lag spikes, saturation appears to drop -> breaker closes -> load surges -> breaker opens again.

Allison Grant: Confirming telemetry lag. We had a 45–90s lag on the “in-use GPUs” metric due to a scrape backlog + label explosion from a misconfigured job (separate issue but it means we need breaker logic resilient to lag).

Sergio Costa: I pulled the graphs. The “telemetry_lag_seconds” panel hits 80s right before the first breaker close. After that, every close aligns with lag spikes. Also note the neighbor p99 delta is spiky because low-volume tenants swing a lot.

Vanessa Ortiz: Fleet note: the pool wasn’t actually “free” when the breaker thought it was. Allocator had outstanding placements but telemetry said capacity recovered. That’s why we saw queue depth rising even when breaker closed.

Jordan Lee: Design-level finding: breaker state machine is currently too eager to close. It treats “below threshold for N samples” as recovery, but samples aren’t independent when the inputs are stale.
Proposal: incorporate a “staleness budget” into the policy evaluation. If either saturation input OR neighbor-impact input is stale beyond X, we should bias toward safety (stay open / reduce burst caps) rather than closing.

Ethan Park: +1 and we can enforce determinism. Right now, two requests that land on different admission controller instances can see different breaker states during transitions (because state propagation is eventual). For GA we probably need:
- a single source of truth for breaker state per pool (or strongly consistent cached value w/ TTL)
- explicit “decision_epoch” so routing can reason about changes.

Mina Haddad: From Smart Routing view: we need denial semantics to be consistent across breaker states. Today we do:
- some denials return retryable 429 w/ `Retry-After`
- some return non-retryable `burst_denied` w/ reason
Customers will implement different retry loops and that changes load. For GA, breaker-open should return a predictable response shape and recommended backoff.

Lauren Bishop: Product ask: whatever we do, we need something CS can explain in one sentence. “Burst temporarily unavailable due to fleet safety; baseline unaffected.” The flapping undermines trust.

Talia Benson: Can we capture action items with owners + target dates? Goal is to have these landed before the GA staged rollout gate.

Rafael Mendes: Findings (proposed):
1) Circuit breaker close criteria doesn’t account for telemetry staleness; closes too early.
2) No minimum-open time / cooldown, leading to flapping and retry amplification.
3) Denial semantics aren’t uniform (retryable vs non-retryable), increasing client-driven load during breaker transitions.
4) Neighbor-impact signal is noisy for low-volume tenants; needs smoothing and “minimum sample” gating.
5) Breaker state propagation can be inconsistent across admission controller replicas.

Sean Gallagher: Agree with those 5.

Peter Holtz: + add “routing fallback behavior during breaker open must be deterministic.” I saw cases where fallback landed on a different model variant due to capacity heuristics. That’s probably okay, but it should be explicit when breaker is open.

Rafael Mendes: Action items draft (please edit):
A) Add telemetry staleness guard: if `telemetry_lag_seconds > X` OR allocator heartbeat stale, breaker cannot close; optionally force open. Owner: Allison + Jordan. Target: end of week.
B) Minimum-open window + exponential recovery: once open, stay open >= 5 min; on recovery, ramp burst caps up gradually (not immediate close). Owner: Keiko + Peter. Target: next sprint.
C) Uniform denial contract for breaker-open state: single reason code (`FLEET_SAFETY_OPEN`), always include `Retry-After` with jitter guidance. Owner: Mina + Ethan. Target: next sprint.
D) Neighbor-impact smoothing + sample threshold: require min request volume per tenant before considering tail deltas; use EWMA and clamp spikes. Owner: Sergio + Allison. Target: next sprint.
E) Stronger breaker state consistency: publish breaker state in control plane/policy engine w/ versioned epoch; replicas read via same cache key w/ TTL, no local recompute. Owner: Ethan + Jordan. Target: design by mid-next-week, implement following.
F) Oncall runbook update: add “breaker flapping” section and immediate mitigation (force-open + cap reduction) w/ commands. Owner: Rafael + Sean. Target: this week.

Allison Grant: For (A)/(D): we already added smoothing in the hotfix branch for telemetry lag denial starvation (related). We can extend that pattern to breaker close logic. I’ll open a small PR with:
- `telemetry_lag_seconds` label reduced cardinality (pool-level only)
- a policy rule: `if lag > 30s => breaker_state = OPEN` (or `HOLD_OPEN`)
We should be careful about false positives though.

Jordan Lee: I’m ok with “HOLD_OPEN” vs “force open” to avoid triggering every time scrapes hiccup. But in this incident, we needed “stay open longer” not “open immediately.” Maybe:
- if OPEN, do not transition to CLOSED unless lag < 15s for 3 consecutive minutes
- if CLOSED, allow OPEN on either (saturation high) OR (neighbor-impact high), regardless of lag.

Keiko Yamamoto: For (B): we can implement a simple hysteresis + cooldown:
- thresholds: open at 0.92 saturation, close at 0.75 (plus lag gate)
- min open 5m
- close requires both saturation low + neighbor-impact normal
Also, “ramp up” can be token-bucket refill rate adjustments rather than binary breaker.

Peter Holtz: Works for routing too. If breaker is OPEN but admission controller still returns some admits due to “ramp,” routing needs to be told the effective cap is reduced, otherwise it’ll keep pushing.

Ethan Park: For (E): we can store breaker state in the same KV we use for pool config snapshots (already versioned). Admission controller reads snapshot at start of request evaluation (single read). That gives determinism within a request.
We still need a writer. Who owns the writer loop? admission controller itself, or separate “breaker manager”?

Vanessa Ortiz: Please not a separate service right now. If admission controller writes breaker state per pool based on inputs, that’s fine, but make sure it’s rate-limited and won’t DDoS the KV store.

Sean Gallagher: + if admission controller is the writer, we need to ensure it still works during partial outage (KV degraded). Default should be “safer”: open / reduce caps.

Mina Haddad: For (C): strongly prefer “always retryable with backoff” for breaker open? But we also need to prevent retry storms.
Maybe:
- return 429 with `Retry-After: 2` (or computed)
- include body field `retryable=true` and reason code
- for some reasons (tenant cap reached) return 429 but with longer retry after

Rafael Mendes: For GA readiness, Support asked for stable reason codes. So +1 on a single code for breaker-open, and keep other codes for tenant cap / cooldown / pool saturated.

Sergio Costa: For (D): we should compute neighbor impact at pool-level (aggregate) rather than tenant-by-tenant deltas. Tenant deltas are useful for forensics, but breaker shouldn’t trip on a tiny tenant’s p99 spike.

Allison Grant: Agree. Breaker signal should be something like: “non-burst p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.25 for 3 min” computed over all non-burst tenants in the pool.

Peter Holtz: That matches how routing thinks about it too.

Talia Benson: Can we lock owners?
- (A) Allison/Jordan
- (B) Keiko/Peter
- (C) Mina/Ethan
- (D) Sergio/Allison
- (E) Ethan/Jordan
- (F) Rafael/Sean

Lauren Bishop: Please add “customer comms snippet” to the runbook or enablement doc. CS will need exact language on flapping mitigation / expectations.

Rafael Mendes: Good call. Adding:
G) Customer-facing comms template for breaker-open periods (beta + GA). Owner: Lauren + Rachel (cc). Target: next week.

Sean Gallagher: Also add gating:
H) Rollout gate: if non-burst p95 regresses > 10% for 10m in any region, automatically hold burst at 0% and page. (I think this is already in-flight but we should track it.) Owner: Sean + Peter. Target: before GA.

Rafael Mendes: Captured.

Harish Reddy: Fleet ops note: for testing, we should replay a synthetic burst with induced telemetry lag (scrape backpressure) to validate “no flapping.” Put that into game day runbook.

Rafael Mendes: Nice. Adding:
I) Game day scenario: induced telemetry lag + burst spike; validate breaker stays open and denial contract stable; ensure baseline SLO holds. Owner: Rafael + Keiko + Allison. Target: before next game day.

Jordan Lee: I’ll start a design doc comment for “breaker state machine v2” with the HOLD_OPEN + hysteresis rules and staleness gates. Will link here.

Ethan Park: I’ll open an ENG ticket for the state consistency (epoch + snapshot read). We should tie it to the existing fleet safety cap work so it doesn’t drift.

Sergio Costa: I’ll update the dashboard panels to show breaker state transitions as annotations + include telemetry lag overlay by default. Would’ve made this 5x faster.

Rafael Mendes: Great. Please paste links to tickets/PRs in-thread as they go up so we can close the loop.

Sean Gallagher: One more: we should explicitly document “breaker-open does not affect baseline Dedicated capacity” and ensure that’s true in routing. During incident, a few baseline requests got 429 due to shared gateway overload policy. Might be separate but worth tracking.

Peter Holtz: I saw that too. It’s gateway-level overload protection, not the burst breaker. But we should align so baseline has higher priority when breaker opens.

Rafael Mendes: Adding:
J) Ensure baseline traffic priority is preserved when breaker opens (gateway + routing). Owner: Peter + Mina. Target: next sprint.

Rafael Mendes: Current action list: A–J above. I’ll summarize into the formal postmortem doc after folks add ticket links. :memo:
